implementation_notes: The stdlib's inline extension `use` executes the block on the resource and closes it whichever way the block finishes; if the block throws and close() also throws, the close exception is attached to the block's exception as a suppressed exception (documented, since Kotlin 1.2 on the JVM and 2.0 for the common AutoCloseable overload), so the guard object collapses into a single method call at the point of acquisition. For actions that are not Closeable/AutoCloseable - rollback, restoring a flag, ending a span - the substitute is try/finally, or `use` on a lightweight AutoCloseable wrapper when the action must compose with other resources; a hand-written guard class is only justified when the action is reused or carries state.
pitfalls: `use` only accepts Closeable/AutoCloseable: arbitrary cleanup needs try/finally, and adding a finally next to a `use` on the same resource double-closes it.
A close() that throws is suppressed behind the block's exception, so a flush-on-close failure is invisible unless it is handled explicitly inside or around the block.
Kotlin has no checked exceptions, so nothing forces a caller to notice that the guard was omitted; lint rules and review are the only enforcement.
